newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia March palm oil output seen up 28-30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia March palm oil output seen up 28-30 pct.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil output in March was estimated to have risen by 28 to 30 precent over February, plantation houses said on Friday.
Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA), which is scheduled to release March crop data on April 15, said February's output was 503,436 tonnes.
"February was a short month and the backlog in harvesting was carried over to March," an official at a plantation house said.
"Also, the output uptrend has begun. We expect more harvesting in coming months and supplies will be flowing into the market," he said.
Palm oil production normally peaks at around October/November.
Ivan Wong, a private crop forecaster, has earlier projected a 32 percent rise in March output to 663,000 tonnes.
Traders have estimated end-March stocks at 725,000 to 730,000 tonnes against end-February's 722,993 tonnes.
Exports in March were estimated at 550,000-570,000 tonnes against PORLA's 376,885 tonnes in February.
-- Tan Lee Lee, Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230-7510)
